## Intent
Hypothesis: scalar per-particle processing with branchy respawn and identity ordering can approach the streaming ceiling on low-churn workloads through sequential access locality.

## Cache saturation
Working set is 68·N, with L1d spill at N≈963 and L2 spill at N≈61680. The measured range begins at N=10000 (680 KB, L2-resident). At death_q=0.01, cost FALLS from 8.61 ns/p (N=10000) to 7.815 ns/p (N=100000, just past the L2→DRAM spill) and keeps falling to 7.429 ns/p at N=10000000 — no cache-spill knee appears; overhead amortization dominates. Higher death rates raise the floor (9.2 ns/p at q=0.1, 11.3 at q=0.25, 13.6 at q=0.5) but the N-shape stays FLAT across all four N values, so death rate lifts the floor without introducing any cache-dependent structure.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 9.15 GB/s at N=10000000, death_q=0.01 — 30.6% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling. At death_q=0.5 it drops to 4.98 GB/s (16.7%). The algo is never bandwidth-bound: at low churn, compute dominates (70.9–72.5% of cycles at q=0.01), making it compute-bound; as death rate rises, branch_flush takes over (20.8% at q=0.1 vs. 14.2% backend_stall), shifting to branch-bound by q=0.1 and reaching 36.2% branch_flush at q=0.5. Bandwidth never approaches the ceiling in any regime.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize. The sole vector-suffixed instruction is `movi.2d v10, #0` (zero init), not SIMD compute. All floating-point work is scalar: `ldr s0`, `fmul s1, s1, s8`, `fadd s0, s0, s1`, `str s0` — one component at a time. No gather (`ld1.s {vN}[i]`) and no `ldr q` 128-bit load exists; `ldp s5, s6` loads adjacent floats into scalar registers, not SIMD lanes. The scatter/deposit path uses byte-granular `ldrb` (12) and `strb` (19) with `csel` (18) for clamping, confirming the branchy respawn's de-vec control. Scalar `ldr s`/`str s` touching 68 bytes/particle through narrow accesses, plus `strb` scatter writes, explain why bandwidth stays at 30.6% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the algo never exceeds 9.15 GB/s (30.6% of the 29.9 GB/s ceiling) at death_q=0.01, N=10000000, and falls to 4.98 GB/s (16.7%) at death_q=0.5. The all-scalar codegen (zero SIMD compute, every `fmul`/`fadd` on `s` registers) and branchy respawn (branch_flush rising to 36.2% at q=0.5) prevent any approach to the streaming ceiling. Identity ordering's sequential locality cannot compensate for the lack of vectorization.
